title: Test recovery at every effect/checkpoint boundary

blocks.text: A crash after an effect but before its checkpoint is safe only when replayed effects are idempotent. The task is: Simulate crash/recovery at before_effect, after_effect, or after_checkpoint for ONE logical operation. Persistent state is modeled by dictionaries outside the restarted worker. Return effect_count and checkpoint_done after recovery. An idempotent mock service prevents duplicate effects; a non-idempotent service demonstrates the after-effect gap. This is a deterministic boundary simulation, not process-crash integration testing.

The inputs are `crash_at`, `idempotent`. Keep their roles separate while you trace the solution. The animation follows the supplied implementation, so every highlighted operation connects to code you can inspect.

blocks.text: Read each symbol as a value with a specific axis, time, rank, token, or state role. The code must preserve those roles. A compact formula does not remove the validation, masking, boundary, or state rules in the prompt.

Before following the implementation, identify the output's shape and meaning. Then identify which input values can affect one selected output. This gives you a testable mental model before the code adds implementation detail.
What changes in the boundary case

This is a deterministic boundary simulation, not process-crash integration testing. Use the Trace control to switch between the normal path and this boundary focus. The algorithm does not get permission to invent an unstated fallback.

A useful test changes one condition while holding the remaining inputs fixed. Compare the output shape, state transition, valid edges, selected tokens, or returned status. This isolates the reason for the change.
